## Where the evidence lives

Start at `cc2340r5/README.md`, then `cc2340r5/FAQ.md` for each problem with its exact error and fix, and `cc2340r5/matrix/README.md` for the stack verdicts. Rows are in `data/results/cc2340r5.csv`. If this file is wrong about your board, correct the FAQ first.

<!-- recovery:start -->
## When the board stops answering

Checked 2026-10-25. Before flashing a risky image, run `python3 tools/preflight_image.py <board id> <image.out>`. Narrative and commands: `docs/remote-board-recovery.md`.

How it locks up:

- The probe is not fully seated: The target failed to see a correctly formatted SWD header (`cc2340r5/FAQ.md`, `cc2340r5/AGENTS.md`)
- An image whose CCFG turns off debug access or chip erase (no image built here did) (`cc2340r5/FAQ.md`)

Try in this order. Remote means the Mac does it with the board in place; hands means a person unplugs, presses or moves something.

| Method | Remote or hands | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pull the probe off the LaunchPad, press it on firmly, replug USB, then flash (the error stayed through a corrected ccxml and slower clocks until the reseat) | hands | proven | `cc2340r5/FAQ.md`, date not recorded |
| UniFlash cc23xx-unlock-debug-access (Failed: Connect failed, twice, while the probe was badly seated; whether it recovers a locked chip is not known) | remote | failed | `cc2340r5/FAQ.md`, `cc2340r5/AGENTS.md`, date not recorded |

<!-- recovery:end -->

==============================================================================
FILE: cc2340r5/baremetal/README.md | How fast is the TI LP-EM-CC2340R5 (CC2340R52) on bare metal with TI Arm Clang?
==============================================================================

# How fast is the TI LP-EM-CC2340R5 (CC2340R52) on bare metal with TI Arm Clang?

Terms: CoreMark, SysTick, NVIC, VIMS and CCFG are defined below and in [docs/vocab.md](../../docs/vocab.md). Errors and fixes: [FAQ.md](../FAQ.md).

EEMBC CoreMark scores 111.09 at -O3 (2.31 per MHz at 48 MHz) and 57.54 at -Oz, with TI Arm Clang 5.1.1 and no operating system, measured on the board on 2026-10-05. Interrupt latency from pend to handler is 28 to 29 CPU cycles (about 0.6 microseconds at 48 MHz), and a GPIO register toggle takes 2.1 cycles per loop pass at -O3.

Built and flashed from an Intel Mac (macOS 15.7.9) with SimpleLink Low Power F3 SDK 9.21.00.36, SysConfig 1.26.3 and UniFlash 9.6.0. The board carries the CC2340R52 chip, 36 kB of RAM; the CC2340R53 is a 64 kB version on a separate board, LP-EM-CC2340R53. 1 kB = 1,024 bytes.

Contents: [results](#results-measured-2026-10-05), [run it](#run-it), [recipe](#recipe), [what it measures](#what-it-measures), [memory](#memory-from-the-linker-map-memory-configuration), [what to do next](#what-to-do-next), [files](#files).

Words used on this page (more in [docs/vocab.md](../../docs/vocab.md)):

- **CoreMark**: EEMBC's standard benchmark for small processors. Higher is faster; "per MHz" divides out the clock so chips at different speeds compare.
- **SysTick**: the Arm core's built-in 24-bit timer. Here it counts every CPU cycle.
- **VIMS**: the CC23xx flash cache and prefetch unit, between the CPU and flash.
- **NVIC**: the Arm core's interrupt controller.

## Results, measured 2026-10-05

| | -O3 | -Oz |
|---|--:|--:|
| CoreMark, iterations per second | **111.09** | 57.54 |
| CoreMark per MHz | **2.31** | 1.20 |
| GPIO toggle, TI driver call, cycles | 19.2 | 31.0 |
| GPIO toggle, register write in a loop, cycles | 2.1 | 9.0 |
| One register write (16 back-to-back), cycles | 2.0 | 2.25 |
| Interrupt latency, pend to handler, direct vector, cycles (includes one SysTick read) | 29 | 28 |
| Flash used (measured build) | 36.8 kB | 25.6 kB |

Each build was run once (measured once); the loop rows are the best of 5 passes within that run. Both runs pass CoreMark's own check ("Correct operation validated", crcfinal 0x4983). Clock read back as 48 MHz (`ClockP_getCpuFreq`); a short host-timed check of the cycle counter gave 48.02 and 48.07 MHz, which agrees but over only 0.3 s. Flash wait states read live from the chip: 2 (1T) and 2 (2T), the factory-trimmed values. Cache, prefetch and micropredictor on (`CCHCTRL` 0x7). Interrupt latency was the same on all 200 tries in each build.

How it compares:

- **Against Arm's figure.** Arm's published CoreMark for the Cortex-M0+ is 2.46 per MHz (Arm Application Note 350, CoreMark on Cortex processors). 2.31 is 94% of it, with flash wait states in the path.
- **Against the MSPM0G3507**, same core, same compiler: 2.46 per MHz at 32 MHz and 2.30 at 80 MHz (rows `coremark_per_mhz` in `data/results/mspm0g3507.csv`). The two chips land within 1% of each other per MHz at full speed.
- **Against Zephyr with GCC on this same chip** (`coremark` rows in `data/results/cc2340r5.csv`): CoreMark 84.07 there (the build named O3, which is really -O2 with loop unrolling), 111.09 here, 32% more. That comparison changes the compiler and the operating system at once, and Zephyr's timer setup on this chip as well, so the 32% is not the compiler alone.

Every number above is a row in `data/results/cc2340r5.csv`.

## Run it

Run from this folder. `--build-only` touches no hardware.

```bash
./run.sh O3 --build-only
```

```bash
./run.sh Oz --build-only
```

```bash
./run.sh O3
```

```bash
./run.sh Oz
```

The first two build and check the CCFG. The last two also flash with UniFlash and capture the serial output to `results/run-<variant>.txt` (a folder the script makes). Flashing runs `/Applications/ti/uniflash_9.6.0/dslite.sh --mode flash -c <connection file> -e -f -u build-<variant>/bench.hex` after a listener opens `/dev/cu.usbmodem<probe serial>1` at 115200. The connection file is the board folder's `CC2340R5.ccxml`; `run.sh` names its full path in the `CCXML` line near the top, so change that line if your copy of the repo is somewhere else. Change the probe serial in the connection file, and the port name (`SERIAL_DEV`), to match yours. `-e` prints progress messages; it is `--verbose`, not erase. Capture stops at `BENCH DONE` or after 300 seconds. The script also saves the host time for every line, for the clock check below.

The script refuses to flash unless the generated `ti_devices_config.c` has `allowDebugPort`, `allowChipErase`, `allowFlashProgram` and `allowReturnToFactory` all `CCFG_PERMISSION_ALLOW`.

**Our mistake, now fixed in `run.sh`:** the first -Oz capture stopped on the previous program's `BENCH DONE` line, because the old program repeats its report every 10 seconds, and saved the wrong run. The listener now waits for a `BENCH DONE` that follows this build's own `I,optimization` line.

## Recipe

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Board | LP-EM-CC2340R5 (CC2340R52: Arm Cortex-M0+, 512 kB flash, 36 kB RAM), XDS110 probe. Board revision: not recorded |
| SDK | SimpleLink Low Power F3 SDK 9.21.00.36 LTS, NoRTOS |
| Starting point | `examples/nortos/LP_EM_CC2340R5/drivers/empty` (ticlang makefile and linker file) |
| SysConfig | 1.26.3 CLI |
| Compiler | TI Arm Clang 5.1.1.LTS (from CCStudio 21.0.1) |
| Flags | `-O3` or `-Oz`, plus `-mcpu=cortex-m0plus -march=thumbv6m -mfloat-abi=soft -mthumb -Wall -gdwarf-3` and the SysConfig `.opt` file, as in the SDK makefile |
| CoreMark | EEMBC sources unmodified (commit 1f483d5, SHA-1 in `coremark/coremark-source.sha1`), new `core_portme.c/.h`. `PERFORMANCE_RUN` (seeds 0, 0, 0x66), `MEM_STACK`, 2k iterations |
| Code location | Flash. No `.TI.ramfunc` section in either map |
| CPU clock | 48 MHz, SysConfig default. `ClockP_CPU_FREQ` is 48000000 for CC23X0 in `kernel/nortos/dpl/ClockPLPF3.h`, printed at run time from `ClockP_getCpuFreq()` |
| Flash wait states | Not set by this program. `hw_fcfg.h` says the factory trim is "Flash 1T wait states (default: 2 WS trimmed)" and "Flash 2T wait states (default: 5 WS untrimmed, 2 WS trimmed)". The program prints the live `VIMS.FLWS1T`, `VIMS.FLWS2T` and the factory trim values (`I,vims_flws1t`, `I,fcfg_flws1t` and so on) |
| Cache | VIMS has a cache, prefetch and micropredictor (`VIMS.CCHCTRL`, `hw_vims.h`). Not set by this program; the live register is printed as `I,vims_cchctrl` |
| CCFG | SysConfig default, byte-identical to the stock `empty` example's generated `ti_devices_config.c` (diffed 2026-10-05) |
| Power | `PowerLPF3_DISALLOW_STANDBY` and `PowerLPF3_DISALLOW_IDLE` constraints set, so the CPU never sleeps and SysTick counts every cycle |
| Supply | USB, through the LaunchPad. Not measured |
| Timer | SysTick on the CPU clock, 24-bit, with a wrap counter: one tick is one CPU cycle (`bench_timer.h`) |
| Date | Built 2026-10-05 |

Changes from the SDK `empty` example, all of them:

1. `bench.syscfg` is `empty.syscfg` plus the four UART2 lines copied from the SDK's `uart2echo.syscfg` (XDS110 backchannel UART).
2. `lpf3_nortos.cmd`: stack 1 kB raised to 4 kB, because CoreMark keeps its 2 kB work area on the stack. Heap stays at the SDK's 8 kB.
3. `makefile`: more source files, `OPT` instead of the fixed `-Oz`, runs from `build-<variant>/`, and `-Wl,--search_path=.` so the linker file finds the generated `.genmap`.
4. `bench.c` replaces `empty.c`. `main_nortos.c` is the SDK's, unchanged.

This follows the project's benchmark method ([docs/methodology.md](../../docs/methodology.md), section 11) and mirrors the MSPM0G3507 bare-metal work in [mspm0g3507/mcu-bench/baremetal/](../../mspm0g3507/mcu-bench/baremetal/).

## What it measures

Same method as the MSPM0G3507 bare-metal pass: loops timed by the cycle counter, best of 5.

| Row | What |
|---|---|
| `timer_read` | one `bench_cycles()` call |
| `empty_loop` | loop overhead |
| `gpio_toggle_driver` | `GPIO_toggle(CONFIG_GPIO_LED_0)`, the TI driver call |
| `gpio_toggle_register` | direct write to `GPIO.DOUTTGL31_0` in a loop |
| `gpio_toggle_str16` | one write to `DOUTTGL31_0`: 16 back-to-back STR in inline asm, minus a SysTick read pair |
| `systick_read_pair` | two back-to-back SysTick reads |
| `irq_latency_best`, `_worst_of_200` | pend LRFD IRQ0 (IRQ 6, the line the Zephyr run used) through the NVIC, read SysTick as the handler's first line. Direct vector, installed with `HwiP_plug`, no wrapper |

The LED used is the SDK's `LED0`, DIO14 (red). The Zephyr run toggled DIO15 (green). Same register either way.

Output on the XDS110 UART at 115200, in the shared benchmark program's format: `BENCH START`, `I,key,value` lines, `R,name,cycles,iterations,description` lines, CoreMark's own report (including `crclist`, `crcmatrix`, `crcstate`, `crcfinal` and "Correct operation validated"), then `BENCH DONE`. The whole report repeats every 10 seconds, with `I,pass,<n>`.

Clock check: `I,cycles_now` is printed at the start and end of each report. Cycles between two passes divided by the host seconds between those lines gives the real CPU clock.

## Memory, from the linker map MEMORY CONFIGURATION

| Build | Flash used, of 512 kB | SRAM used, of 36 kB | CCFG |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| -O3 | 36.8 kB (0x9318) in the measured build; 36.6 kB (0x9244) after the rebuild that removed the compiler's version string | 15.8 kB (0x3F02) | 2 kB |
| -Oz | 25.6 kB (0x6692) in the measured build; 25.4 kB (0x65BE) after the rebuild | 15.8 kB (0x3F02) | 2 kB |

SRAM includes the 8 kB heap and the 4 kB stack, both reserved, not used. Whole program; split by component is not done.

## What to do next

- Energy per CoreMark iteration and sleep current need a power meter. **Tool or docs:** the LP-XDS110ET probe's EnergyTrace has no Mac support.
- Split the memory figures by component.

## Files

| File | From |
|---|---|
| `bench.c`, `bench_timer.h`, `coremark/core_portme.c`, `coremark/core_portme.h` | written here |
| `main_nortos.c` | SDK `empty` example, unchanged |
| `bench.syscfg`, `lpf3_nortos.cmd`, `makefile` | SDK `empty` example, changed as listed above |
| `coremark/core_*.c`, `coremark/coremark.h`, `LICENSE.md` | EEMBC, unmodified |
| `run.sh` | build, check, flash, capture |

FILE: cc2340r5/ble-light/README.md | Bluetooth light on the LP-EM-CC2340R5 (CC2340R52)

# Bluetooth light on the LP-EM-CC2340R5 (CC2340R52)

Terms: [docs/vocab.md](../../docs/vocab.md). Errors and fixes: [FAQ.md](../FAQ.md). Status: Should work. The firmware builds for this board and has not run on it.

A phone page controls the kit's LEDs over Bluetooth Low Energy. It is the same firmware as the CC2755P10 one, built from the same source. The service UUID, characteristics, LED pins and what is untested are in [cc2755p10/ble-light/README.md](../../cc2755p10/ble-light/README.md).

Build it from the top of the repository:

```bash
cc2340r5/ble-light/build.sh
```

The output lands in `prebuilt/cc2340r5/ble-light/`. The LEDs are red on DIO14 and green on DIO15. Built 2026-10-15 with SimpleLink Low Power F3 SDK 9.21.00.36.

Next: flash it, then connect from a phone browser that supports Web Bluetooth and write a color.

==============================================================================

# Bluetooth desk display (LP-EM-CC2340R5 + SSD1306 OLED)

Status: firmware flashed and booting; Bluetooth echo and display not yet run. Evidence: [experiment page](../../docs/experiments/2026-10-30-cc2340r5-desk-display.md).

![Four wires](img/wiring.png)

| Wire | LaunchPad end | OLED end |
|---|---|---|
| Power | J1 pin 1 (3V3) | VCC |
| Ground | J3 pin 22 (GND) | GND |
| Clock | J1 pin 9 (DIO24, I2C_SCL) | SCL |
| Data | J1 pin 10 (DIO0, I2C_SDA) | SDA |

Run, after wiring and with USB plugged in (one venv once: `python3 -m venv ~/.venvs/ble && ~/.venvs/ble/bin/pip install bleak`):

```bash
DESK_LAT=<lat> DESK_LON=<lon> cc2340r5/desk-display/run.sh clock    # time, date, weather on the OLED
cc2340r5/desk-display/run.sh page                                    # browser page at http://localhost:8000/ (stop the clock first: one link at a time)
cc2340r5/desk-display/run.sh test                                    # three lines, echo check, no display needed
```

Rebuild and flash: `cc2340r5/desk-display/build.sh`, then DSLite with `cc2340r5/CC2340R5.ccxml -e -f -u out/frl_desk_cc2340r5.hex`. Back up first (cc2340r5/AGENTS.md). Restore is the same page's restore recipe.

If the Mac's Bluetooth stops answering after a connect: turn Bluetooth off and on in Control Center (cc2340r5/AGENTS.md).

FILE: cc2340r5/matrix/README.md | What works on the TI LP-EM-CC2340R5, and where does each radio stack stop?

# What works on the TI LP-EM-CC2340R5, and where does each radio stack stop?

Terms: RCP, DMM, OTA, ZHA, MCUboot and CCFG are defined in [docs/vocab.md](../../docs/vocab.md). Errors and fixes: [FAQ.md](../FAQ.md).

Bluetooth LE and a Zigbee router into Home Assistant work on this board from TI's SimpleLink Low Power F3 SDK 9.21.00.36 examples, with a few settings changed. Most of the rest fails to link for lack of RAM (the chip has 36 kB) with TI's configurations, and the remainder stops at a missing TI port or a fault not found.

In six lines:

1. **Works:** Bluetooth LE (advertise, connect, echo) and a Zigbee router into Home Assistant. A Zigbee end device (TI's on/off switch example) rejoined the network 15 s after flashing, measured once; its device type and sleep behavior were not confirmed. TI's OTA client example, also an end device, joined and was listed as an end device.
2. **RAM decides:** 36 kB. Left for your code: 5.1 kB with Bluetooth, 6.2 kB with a Zigbee end device, 10.7 kB with the Zigbee OTA client, 8.8 kB with the Thread RCP (flashed and run, 2026-10-06), 799 B with a Zigbee router with logging on.
3. **Compiles, fails to link (RAM):** a full Thread device (7.5 kB to 23.8 kB over, depending on build options) and Bluetooth plus 802.15.4 at once (DMM, 2.1 kB short of the chip's total free RAM before any heap). **Unknown (suspected: Chip limit):** only TI's configurations were tried, built with this repo's settings; a trimmed build might fit; not run. Both link on the 64 kB CC2340R53.
4. **Builds, does not run:** Bluetooth on TI's Zephyr fork. hello_world ran after a boot-configuration change; Bluetooth samples printed nothing. **Unknown.**
5. **Starts, never finishes:** a Zigbee over-the-air update from Home Assistant. Best 1.34% in four transfers. **Unknown (suspected: Radio environment).**
6. **Not offered for this chip:** Matter, Thread under Zephyr, Bluetooth under upstream Zephyr. ESPHome's Zigbee end device links (32.0 kB of the 36 kB of RAM; not run); its router build is 1.3 kB over.

Tested 2026-10-05 into 2026-10-06 on one board with an XDS110 probe, from an Intel MacBook (macOS 15.7.9) with TI Arm Clang 5.1.1, SysConfig 1.26.3 and UniFlash 9.6.0; Home Assistant ran ZHA with a ZBT-2 radio on a separate host. The board carries the CC2340R52 chip (36 kB of RAM); the 64 kB CC2340R53 is on a separate board, LP-EM-CC2340R53. 1 kB = 1,024 bytes.

## Verdict for each combination

| Combination | Verdict | Cause | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bluetooth LE, TI SDK | **Works** | | Advertised, connected, echo checked |
| Bluetooth LE, upstream Zephyr 4.4.2 | **No** | **Third-party behavior** | Board file lists GPIO and UART only |
| Bluetooth LE, TI's Zephyr fork | **Builds; Bluetooth samples print nothing** | **Unknown** | hello_world ran after a boot-configuration change (CCFG byte 0x4E02001C); Bluetooth samples printed nothing ([zephyr-ti](../zephyr-ti/README.md)) |
| Zigbee router, TI SDK | **Works** | | Joined Home Assistant; 20 of 20 commands landed; 95 ms median at first pairing; about 5 s after re-pairing, cause unknown ([zigbee](../zigbee/README.md)) |
| Zigbee end device, TI SDK | **Joined; type confirmed only for the OTA client example** | **Unknown** (type, sleep) | `onoff_switch` rejoined 15 s after flashing, measured once; Home Assistant kept its old router record |
| Bluetooth plus 802.15.4 at once (DMM) | **Compiles, fails to link (RAM) on the R52; links on the R53** | **Unknown (suspected: Chip limit)** | 2.1 kB short of the chip's total free RAM before any heap; a trimmed build might fit; not run |
| Thread | **RCP only per TI; RCP flashed and run (joined a CC1354P10 leader, 2026-10-06); node builds fail to link (RAM)** | **Unknown (suspected: Chip limit)** | Node builds 7.5 kB to 23.8 kB over, depending on build options; a trimmed build might fit; not run ([thread](../thread/README.md)) |
| Thread, Zephyr | **No** | **Tool or docs** | No 802.15.4 driver for CC23xx in TI's fork |
| Matter | **No** | **Tool or docs** | TI's Matter fork has CC27xx examples only; not built |
| Proprietary 2.4 GHz packets | **Builds** | | `rfPacketTx`; not run, needs a second radio |
| Bluetooth over-the-air update | **Works from a Mac** | | One run on 2026-10-07 with this repo's `tools/oad/oad_client.py` and TI's dual-image example; TI's own senders are a phone app or a Windows program ([oad](../oad/README.md)) |
| Zigbee over-the-air update | **Starts, never finishes** | **Unknown (suspected: Radio environment)** | Best 1.34% of 200.1 kB |
| SysConfig without the GUI | **Works** | | About seven settings tried as `.syscfg` text edits; Bluetooth changes seen on air |
| ESPHome | **End device links, not run; router build does not fit** | **Chip limit** | The router build needed 37.4 kB of the 36 kB of RAM ([experiment](../../docs/experiments/2026-10-13-cc2340r5-esphome-fit.md)) |
| Clock speed | **48 MHz** | | TI documents only 48 MHz; read back at 48.0 MHz once |

"No" verdicts say which kind of no: **Tool or docs** when TI offers nothing for this chip, **Chip limit** when the chip cannot (written as suspected when only TI's configurations were tried), **Third-party behavior** when the gap is in non-TI software.

Why the OTA cause is suspected, not proven: the coordinator's readings of this board that evening, none taken during a transfer, were LQI 36 to 48 and RSSI -88 to -91 dBm, a weak link.

## More on this board

- RAM per stack: `memory-breakdown.json` in this folder, and the rows `radio_ram_left` and `radio_flash_used` in `data/results/cc2340r5.csv`.
- Bluetooth, Zigbee and CPU numbers: the same CSV.
- Write-ups: [DMM](../../docs/experiments/2026-10-05-cc2340r5-dmm.md), [Thread](../../docs/experiments/2026-10-05-cc2340r5-thread-full-device.md), [Zigbee OTA](../../docs/experiments/2026-10-05-cc2340r5-zigbee-ota-home-assistant.md), [TI's Zephyr](../../docs/experiments/2026-10-05-cc2340r5-ti-zephyr-ble.md), [SysConfig](../../docs/experiments/2026-10-05-cc2340r5-sysconfig-without-gui.md).

## Not done

Sleep current, energy, packet error rate and range; a full Thread border router with this chip as its radio ([thread](../thread/README.md); the CC2340R5 RCP already drove a CC1354P10 host in [the border-router host](../../border-router/host-cc1354/README.md)); the debugger on TI's Zephyr Bluetooth samples, which print nothing ([zephyr-ti](../zephyr-ti/README.md)).

FILE: cc2340r5/oad/README.md | How do I update a TI LP-EM-CC2340R5 over Bluetooth from a Mac terminal?
==============================================================================

# How do I update a TI LP-EM-CC2340R5 over Bluetooth from a Mac terminal?

Yes for the Bluetooth name and version; the red LED was not watched. The update ran once on 2026-10-07: 31.4 s transfer, 7.8 s to the new name, version 2.0.0 read back. One run.

That is about 41 s from scan to new name (the sum of the saved timings: scan 0.84 s, connect 0.99 s, transfer 31.44 s, enable to new name 7.78 s), and 43 s including the version read, which the run's JSON output does not log separately. Use TI's dual-image OAD example with TI's prebuilt MCUboot bootloader, and send the new image with [`tools/oad/oad_client.py`](../../tools/oad/oad_client.py), a Python script on the bleak Bluetooth library that speaks TI's OAD protocol. Both images build from the terminal in about two minutes, and a dry run checks the image header, SHA-256, signature and the chip's lock fields with no board.

Terms: OAD, dual image, MCUboot, SHA-256 and ECDSA signature, ATT MTU, bleak, imgtool, 0xFF padding, CCFG and CCFG checksums, OTA and the XDS110 probe are defined in [docs/vocab.md](../../docs/vocab.md). Errors and fixes: [FAQ.md](../FAQ.md). 1 kB = 1,024 bytes.

Time to repeat, once the tools in [mac-setup/README.md](../../mac-setup/README.md) are installed: about 2 minutes to build, about 13 s to flash, under a minute for the update, plus the backup and restore reads (not timed).

OAD (over-the-air download) is TI's name for sending new firmware to a running Bluetooth device. TI documents it with a phone app (SimpleLink Connect) or a Windows tool; this page does it from a Mac terminal.

Contents: [why dual image](#which-oad-flavour-and-why), [what you need](#what-you-need), [build](#build-two-minutes), [the files](#the-files), [dry run](#check-the-image-without-a-board), [expected and measured](#what-was-expected-and-what-was-measured), [on the board](#on-the-board), [the protocol](#the-protocol-as-the-sdk-source-implements-it), [guide against source](#where-tis-guide-and-the-sdk-source-disagree), [can it lock the chip](#can-this-lock-the-chip), [not confirmed](#what-could-not-be-confirmed), [still open](#what-is-still-open).

Checked 2026-10-07 on an Intel MacBook, macOS 15.7.9: SimpleLink Low Power F3 SDK 9.21.00.36 LTS, TI Arm Clang 5.1.1 LTS, SysConfig 1.26.3, UniFlash 9.6.0, Python 3.14.7 with bleak 3.0.2.

## Which OAD flavour, and why

The F3 SDK has three single-image flavours for this board. The build uses **dual image** (`basic_ble_oad_dual_image`).

| Flavour | Where the new image waits | Runs during the download | Fits this board? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Off-chip | External SPI flash (a separate flash chip on the board, wired to the SPI bus) | Your app | No: the LP-EM-CC2340R5 has no external flash fitted |
| On-chip | Internal flash, after your app is erased | A small "persistent" app (`basic_persistent`), a second app that stays on the chip only to receive the new image | Yes, but your app is gone during the download and a second app must be built and flashed |
| Dual image | Internal flash, second half | Your app | Yes: your app keeps running, and only two files go on the chip |

Dual image halves the room for your app: each slot is 236 kB. TI's Bluetooth app uses 192 kB of it, so there is room. The fourth example, multi-step OAD, splits one large app into two halves; it needs a bootloader built with a different option and is a separate test.

## What you need

| Thing | Version used | Where |
|---|---|---|
| LP-EM-CC2340R5 board and an LP-XDS110ET (or LP-XDS110) probe | any serial | <https://www.ti.com/tool/LP-EM-CC2340R5> |
| SimpleLink Low Power F3 SDK, SysConfig, TI Arm Clang, UniFlash | as above | install steps in [mac-setup/README.md](../../mac-setup/README.md) |
| Python 3 with bleak, a Bluetooth library for Python | 3.14.7, bleak 3.0.2 | <https://pypi.org/project/bleak/> |
| A Mac with Bluetooth, and Bluetooth permission for your terminal app | macOS 15.7.9 | System Settings, Privacy and Security, Bluetooth |

Set up once. A Python environment with bleak (here in your home folder, outside the repo):

```bash
python3 -m venv ~/ble && ~/ble/bin/pip install bleak
```

The public key compiled into TI's MCUboot, which the client uses to check the signature. Change the SDK path if yours differs:

```bash
export KEYS=/Applications/ti/simplelink_lowpower_f3_sdk_9_21_00_36_LTS/source/third_party/mcuboot/boot/ti/source/mcuboot_app/keys.c
```

## Build (two minutes)

From the repo root:

```bash
cc2340r5/oad/build.sh
```

The script copies TI's example twice into `build/` (git-ignored), applies [`app.patch`](app.patch), and builds each copy with `make` and TI's own post-build step, which signs the image with MCUboot's `imgtool`. The two copies differ in three ways:

| | v1 (flash with the probe) | v2 (send over the air) |
|---|---|---|
| Advertised name | `FRL OAD 1` | `FRL OAD 2` |
| LED | green, toggles every 1,000 ms | red, toggles every 250 ms |
| Signed version | 1.0.0 | 2.0.0 |

The name is one line in the example's `.syscfg`; the blink is a short patch to `app/app_main.c` (a timer that toggles one LED) that reads its LED and rate from a header the script writes. The build took 65 s for v1 and 49 s for v2, as `build.sh` printed them on 2026-10-07 (observed, not saved). TI's unchanged example took 43.6 s (`real 43.59`). Paths to the SDK and tools are at the top of `build.sh`; change them if yours differ.

## The files

From `images.txt`, which the build script writes with SHA-256 sums:

| File | Bytes | What it is |
|---|--:|---|
| `images/mcuboot_dual_image.hex` | 36,716 | TI's prebuilt MCUboot for dual image, copied from the SDK's `prebuilt_hexfiles`. 13.1 kB of code at 0x0, plus the CCFG |
| `images/frl_oad_v1.bin` | 241,664 | v1, flashed at 0x6000. Header 256 + app 196,564 + signature area 152 (196,564 is the image size field; the linker map's APP_SLOT shows 196,560 used), padded with 0xFF to the slot size |
| `images/frl_oad_v2.bin` | 241,664 | v2, the update. Real content 192.4 kB; 43.6 kB are padding |

Each slot is 0x3B000 bytes: the app slot runs from 0x6000 to 0x41000, the download slot from 0x41000 to 0x7C000, and the Bluetooth bond storage (where the board keeps the keys of devices it has paired with) sits at 0x7D000. MCUboot's own table of slots, read from the hex, says the same. RAM: 32,234 of 36 kB used (from the linker map).

The padding is sent too. TI's post-build adds MCUboot's 16-byte "upgrade waiting" marker at the very end of the slot, and TI's own phone app sends the whole padded file when that marker is there. So 18.5% of the bytes sent are 0xFF.

## Check the image without a board

```text
~/ble/bin/python tools/oad/oad_client.py --dry-run --keys-c $KEYS cc2340r5/oad/images/frl_oad_v2.bin
```

`--keys-c` points at the public key compiled into TI's MCUboot. Output on v2, trimmed:

```text
  img_size          196564
  version           2.0.0+0
  tlvs              ['SHA256 (32 B)', 'KEYHASH (32 B)', 'ECDSA_SIG (70 B)']
  sha256_ok         True
  keyhash_ok        True
  signature_ok      True
  trailer_magic     True
  send_bytes        241664
  identify payload  3db8f396000000000001000000b0030000000000020000000000000000000000
  transfer plan     1024 blocks of 236 data bytes (block size 240 with the 4-byte block number), last block 236 bytes, 245760 bytes written in total
dry run OK: the image parses, its hash and signature check out, and it fits the slot
```

`tlvs` is the list of tagged records MCUboot adds after the app, each a type, a length and a value: `SHA256` is the hash of header and app, `KEYHASH` is the SHA-256 of the public key that signed the image (so MCUboot can tell which key to check with), and `ECDSA_SIG` is the signature. MCUboot images carry no CRC: the check is a SHA-256 of header and app, and an ECDSA P-256 signature over it. The dry run recomputes both, verifies the signature with the key from `keys.c` (in plain Python, no extra packages), and confirms TI's prebuilt MCUboot contains that same key (`images.py haskey`). The check was tested on five broken copies of the file: one flipped bit in the app, in the signature, or in the version field each failed, and a wrong header magic failed. A file cut short after the signature area passed with a printed note that the upgrade marker is missing, which is the right answer: the image is valid, but MCUboot may not install it. All five were refused. TI's `oad_image_tool` and `computeCRC32.py` (in `tools/common/oad`) are for TI's older image format; no CC2340R5 example uses them.

The client's Bluetooth path was also run against a software stand-in for the board, [`tools/oad/sim_target.py`](../../tools/oad/sim_target.py), which follows the state machine in the SDK's `oad_profile.c`. All 1,024 blocks arrived in order, the stand-in's slot matched the file byte for byte, and it came back as `FRL OAD 2` version 2.0.0. With the packet size set to 185 the client stopped before sending a block. This tests the client's logic, not the radio or TI's code.

```text
~/ble/bin/python tools/oad/sim_target.py cc2340r5/oad/images/frl_oad_v2.bin
```

## What was expected, and what was measured

The Expected column was written before the board run. The Measured column is the one run on 2026-10-07; the source of each number is in the cell.

| Step | Expected | Where the expectation comes from | Measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flash MCUboot and v1 | about 10 to 20 s; green LED toggles every second; `FRL OAD 1` advertising | the 7 s blink flash in [../README.md](../README.md), with about 270 kB more to write; an estimate | 13 s for both files in one command (observed on the console, not saved). `FRL OAD 1` seen at -33 dBm in the first 15 s scan (observed, not saved) |
| Packet size the Mac agrees (ATT MTU, the largest data packet per write) | 243 bytes or more, needed for 240-byte blocks | the board allows 251 (`maxPDUSize = 255`); this Mac agreed 65 with an example capped at 65 | 251 (`att_mtu` in the client's JSON output) |
| Transfer, 1,024 blocks | about 46 s; 31 s to 2 minutes | this Mac's 45 ms median write-and-notify round trip, times 1,024 | **31.4 s**, 1,024 blocks of 236 data bytes, no retries |
| Speed | about 40 kbit/s of image data | 236 kB in 46 s | **61.5 kbit/s**: 236 kB in 31.4 s, packet size 251, connect 0.99 s after a 0.84 s scan |
| Enable to `FRL OAD 2` seen | under 15 s | MCUboot copies 236 kB and checks the signature; estimate, no measurement | **7.78 s** from the enable command to the new name advertising; enable status SUCCESS, the link dropped for the reset |
| Version read after the update | 2.0.0 | the signed header | **2.0.0** (raw `020000000000`); the header at 0x6000 reads byte 20 = `02` |
| LED after the update | red, toggling every 250 ms | the patch | not watched; the name, version and header say the new image runs, but the LED itself was not checked |

What could fail, as listed before the run: the Mac agrees a packet size under 243 (the client stops before sending anything, see the protocol section); the Mac's connection interval is longer than 15 ms (slower, not broken); MCUboot does not install the image (marker or version rule; the board then still runs v1); macOS shows the old cached name for the board (the client reads the name from the advertisement, not the cache). None of these happened on the one run: the packet size was 251, MCUboot installed v2, and the client saw the new name. The connection interval was not read.

## On the board

Run these from the repo root, one at a time. `DSLITE` is UniFlash's command-line program; the connection file picks the probe by serial number (put your probe's serial in the `.ccxml` file). `BK` is a backup folder outside the repo; any path works.

```bash
export DSLITE=/Applications/ti/uniflash_9.6.0/deskdb/content/TICloudAgent/osx/ccs_base/DebugServer/bin/DSLite CCXML=cc2340r5/CC2340R5.ccxml BK=$HOME/cc2340r5-oad-backup && mkdir -p $BK
```

1. Back up the whole flash and the CCFG, outside the repo (the board may hold a Zigbee network key). DSLite's `memory -r <address>,<length>` takes the length as a count of 32-bit words, not bytes: 0x20000 is a count of 32-bit words; the file came out 512 kB, the whole 512 kB flash. The CCFG read below, 0x200 words, came out 2 kB. Check the file sizes after your own read.

```text
$DSLITE memory -c $CCXML -r 0x0,0x20000 -o $BK/main_flash.bin
```

```text
$DSLITE memory -c $CCXML -r 0x4E020000,0x200 -o $BK/ccfg.bin
```

```bash
python3 cc2340r5/oad/images.py merge $BK/restore.hex $BK/main_flash.bin@0x0 $BK/ccfg.bin@0x4E020000
```

```bash
python3 cc2340r5/oad/images.py ccfg $BK/restore.hex
```

2. Flash MCUboot and v1 in one command. UniFlash's default for CC23xx chips erases the whole chip at the start of every program load ("Erase Settings during Program Load", default Chip Erase, in `CC23xx_FlashProperties.xml`; see the FAQ), so both files go in the same load. In the command, `-e` is `--verbose` (progress messages), `-f` loads the files to flash, and `-u` runs the program afterwards.

```text
$DSLITE flash -c $CCXML -e -f -u cc2340r5/oad/images/mcuboot_dual_image.hex cc2340r5/oad/images/frl_oad_v1.bin,0x6000
```

Check: the green LED toggles once a second. If the app is flashed without MCUboot, the probe reports error -615 when it tries to run it, as TI's example README describes.

3. Send v2 over the air and check it comes back:

```text
~/ble/bin/python tools/oad/oad_client.py --name "FRL OAD 1" --expect-name "FRL OAD 2" --keys-c $KEYS --json oad-run.json cc2340r5/oad/images/frl_oad_v2.bin
```

It prints the running version, the block size, progress every 5% with kbit/s, the download time, the time from "enable" to the new name, and the new version, and writes the numbers to `oad-run.json`. Then look at the board: red LED, four toggles a second (not watched on the run).

4. Optional second proof, by probe: the image header at 0x6000 holds the version at byte 20. The length 0x8 is 8 words, so the file is 32 bytes.

```text
$DSLITE memory -c $CCXML -r 0x6000,0x8 -o $BK/hdr.bin && xxd $BK/hdr.bin
```

Byte 20 reads `02` after the update and `01` before.

5. Put the board back. The same default chip erase clears the flash first, then the backup is written:

```text
$DSLITE flash -c $CCXML -e -f -u $BK/restore.hex
```

## The protocol, as the SDK source implements it

Service `F000FFC0-0451-4000-B000-000000000000`, on TI's 128-bit base `F000xxxx-0451-4000-B000-000000000000`:

| Characteristic | UUID (short) | Direction | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Image identify | 0xFFC1 | write with response; notify | the image header; 1-byte accept or refuse |
| Image block | 0xFFC2 | write | 4-byte block number, then 236 bytes of the file |
| Control | 0xFFC5 | write without response; notify | commands, replies and block requests |

The sequence the client runs: turn on notifications for 0xFFC1 and 0xFFC5; Get Software Version (`07`); Get Block Size (`01`, reply `01 F0 00` = 240); write the 32-byte image header to 0xFFC1 with its size field set to the bytes being sent; Start (`03`); answer each block request `12 <status> <block number>` with that block; on status 14 (download complete) send Enable Image (`04`); the board replies `04 00`, drops the link, resets, and MCUboot installs the image. Sources: `source/ti/ble/profiles/oad/src/oad_profile.c`, `source/ti/ble/services/oad/src/oad_service.c` and `source/ti/ble/app_util/sw_update/src/sw_update.c` in the SDK, and TI's open-source SimpleLink Connect app (`src/components/FWUpdate/FWUpdate_Modal.tsx` on github.com/TexasInstruments/simplelink-connect).

The block size is fixed at 240 in the source, and the board ignores the offset of a long write, so every block must fit in one write. The client checks the agreed packet size first and stops if a 240-byte block would not fit, with this message from [`tools/oad/oad_client.py`](../../tools/oad/oad_client.py) (the numbers in angle brackets are filled in from the connection):

`ATT MTU <mtu> carries at most <mtu - 3> bytes a write, the target wants 240. The target ignores the offset of a long write, so this would corrupt the image. Stopping.`

## Where TI's guide and the SDK source disagree

The guide is the BLE5-Stack User's Guide in the SDK (`docs/ble5stack/ble_user_guide`, OAD chapter). Where they disagree, the client follows the source. Each row is **Tool or docs**.

| Topic | Guide says | Source does |
|---|---|---|
| Block size | chosen from the agreed packet size, 20 to 244 | always 240 (`OAD_DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE`) |
| Where block requests arrive | notifications on 0xFFC2 | notifications on 0xFFC5; 0xFFC2 never notifies |
| Enable Image `04` | not in the command table | required after the download, or nothing installs |
| Download complete | block number 0xFFFFFFFF | the block count (1,024 here) |
| Commands before image identify | answered with AUTH_FAIL | block size, version and status answered any time; start, enable and cancel get NOT_STARTED |
| Software version reply | 5 bytes | 7 bytes: major, minor, revision (2), build (2) |
| Bytes to send | the header's image size | `ih_img_size` leaves out the header and signature, so a client must replace it; TI's app does, the guide does not say so |
| Header table | `ih_flags` is "total length", `_pad1` is 2 bytes | MCUboot flags; `_pad1` is 4 bytes |

## Can this lock the chip?

Not from these images, as far as the files show. The CCFG was not read back from the chip after the update (not done). **Setup or handling:** the lock fields are set by the CCFG of whatever you flash. The CCFG that reaches the chip here is MCUboot's (the app `.bin` files have none), and in it `allowDebugPort` and `allowChipErase` are both allow (0xA), debug authorization is open (0x5A), and no flash sectors are write-protected; the two app builds' own CCFGs say the same (from `images.txt`). The update itself writes only to the download slot (0x41000 to 0x7BFFF, enforced by the flash driver's region), and MCUboot writes only the app slot, so neither can change the CCFG.

One oddity: TI's prebuilt MCUboot hex has all four CCFG checksums set to zero. **Tool or docs.** UniFlash's default for this chip family rewrites those checksums from the image while flashing (setting "Overwrite CRC fields in CCFG", default on, in `CC23xx_FlashProperties.xml`), so flash it with UniFlash defaults and do not turn that setting off. This was seen on 2026-10-07 flashing TI's prebuilt hex: UniFlash logged `Updating CRC32 field ccfg.crc32 @ address 0x4E02074C ... Value changes from 0x00000000 to 0xB714DFB7`. It rewrote three of the four fields; the log has no line for the user record. The same settings file shows UniFlash skips the CCFG user record by default, which may explain the verify mismatch at 0x4E020750 described in gotcha 8 of the CC2340R5 start-here page ([../README.md](../README.md)); not tested.

## What could not be confirmed

- **Unknown:** which upgrade mode TI's prebuilt MCUboot uses (overwrite or swap) and whether it refuses older versions. No configuration file ships beside the hex. Suspected overwrite, because the app is linked for the first slot only and TI's post-build adds the upgrade marker. v2 is signed 2.0.0 against v1's 1.0.0, so a version rule would not block this test.
- **Unknown:** the connection interval macOS agrees with this board; the client does not read it. The packet size was measured: 251 bytes.
- **Unknown (suspected: Tool or docs):** the linker gives the app slot 0x3B700 bytes from 0x6100, which runs 2 kB past the 0x41000 start of the download slot. `imgtool` would refuse an image too large for the slot, so a build cannot silently overlap; this app uses 192 kB.
- Not tested: writing blocks without response (`--no-response`), which the guide recommends for speed and TI's app does not use.
- One run only. The red LED was not watched. Only this Intel Mac was used.

## What is still open

1. Run the update twice more, for a median of three.
2. Test `--no-response` (blocks written without response) against the same image.
3. Watch the LED after the update: red, four toggles a second.
4. Run the same steps on an Apple Silicon Mac.

==============================================================================
FILE: cc2340r5/thread/README.md | Can the TI LP-EM-CC2340R5 run Thread as an end device or router?
==============================================================================

# Can the TI LP-EM-CC2340R5 run Thread as an end device or router?

Terms: RCP, MTD, FTD, NCP, NVS, CCFG, `.bss` and linker are defined below and in [docs/vocab.md](../../docs/vocab.md). Errors and fixes: [FAQ.md](../FAQ.md).

Not as a Thread node with TI's configurations on this chip: node builds fail to link for lack of RAM. **As a radio co-processor it works** (2026-10-06). The `ot-rcp` image answers OpenThread's POSIX host on the Mac over the debugger UART at **921600 baud** (`OPENTHREAD/1.4.0.0; CC23XX thread-v1.4-ti-1.0-ea-1.0`) once its CCFG checksums are filled (Zephyr's `ti_ccfg_crc32_calculate.py`), it is flashed with DSLite and it is started with a probe reset.

On the CC2340R52 chip (36 kB of RAM) the RCP links with 8.8 kB to spare. Every Thread node build (MTD, FTD, CLI or NCP) compiles, fits in flash, and then fails to link because RAM runs out, by 7.5 to 23.8 kB depending on build options. **Unknown (suspected: Chip limit):** only TI's configurations were tried, built with this repo's settings (GCC 12.2, board checks removed); a trimmed build might fit; not run. The same builds link on the CC2340R53 (64 kB of RAM); the default builds in the table below leave 7.3 to 20.5 kB to spare.

TI's `ot-ti` UART runs at 921600 baud, not 115200. The unreadable output seen earlier from the radio CLI image at 115200 was probably this; it was not rechecked at 921600.

The RAM numbers line up with TI's listing of this board as RCP only, but TI does not state its reason (**Unknown**). TI enforces the listing with a CMake board check, not a memory check (see "The gate").

Built 2026-10-05 on an Intel Mac (macOS 15.7.9) from TI's `ot-ti`, branch `thread-v1.4-ti` (commit `eaac0deb`, the commit tagged as release `thread-v1.4-ti-2.1`). The build pass flashed nothing. Afterward the radio test CLI (`ot-cli-radio`) was flashed once, with its boot checksums filled by upstream Zephyr's script; it answered with bytes that did not decode at 115200 baud and with nothing at other common rates. **Unknown.** That serial output was observed 2026-10-05; not saved.

The board carries the CC2340R52 chip, 36 kB of RAM; the CC2340R53 is a 64 kB version on a separate board, LP-EM-CC2340R53. 1 kB = 1,024 bytes; 1 GB = 1,024 MB.

Words used on this page (more in [docs/vocab.md](../../docs/vocab.md)):

- **RCP**, radio co-processor: only the radio. A bigger computer runs Thread and drives it over a serial link.
- **MTD**, minimal Thread device: an end device. It does not route.
- **FTD**, full Thread device: can route for other devices.
- **NCP**, network co-processor: runs Thread itself and is controlled by a host.
- **NVS**, non-volatile storage: the flash area where Thread keeps its settings across power cycles.

Contents: [results and link errors](#results), [the gate](#the-gate-what-restricts-the-r52-to-rcp), [local edits](#local-edits), [this repo's toolchain differs from TI's](#this-repos-toolchain-differs-from-tis), [CCFG](#ccfg-debug-and-erase), [exact commands](#exact-commands), [attempts](#attempts-and-wall-times), [a huge .bin file](#trap-a-huge-bin-file), [what to do next](#what-to-do-next), [details: output files, tools, disk](#details).

## Results

| Build (target) | Links on the R52 (36 kB)? | Flash used | RAM used | R52: RAM over or under | R53 (64 kB): RAM under |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| RCP (`ot-rcp`) | yes* | 107.1 kB | 27.2 kB | 8.8 kB under | 36.8 kB under |
| Radio CLI (`ot-cli-radio`) | yes* | 96.1 kB | 25.8 kB | 10.2 kB under | 38.2 kB under |
| CLI MTD (`ot-cli-mtd`) | **no** | 353.3 kB | 46 kB | **10 kB over** | 18 kB under |
| CLI FTD (`ot-cli-ftd`) | **no** | 417.5 kB | 52 kB | **16 kB over** | 12 kB under |
| NCP MTD (`ot-ncp-mtd`) | **no** | 342.5 kB | 43.5 kB | **7.5 kB over** | 20.5 kB under |
| NCP FTD (`ot-ncp-ftd`) | **no** | 404.4 kB | 56.7 kB | **20.7 kB over** | 7.3 kB under |

\* Every image, on both chips, links only after the settings-area fix (edit 3 below). That includes the RCP TI lists as supported.

The GNU linker (`ld`) gives two kinds of link error, shown here with its path cut to the file name:

**Before the settings-area fix**, images stop on the settings area. **Unknown (suspected: Tool or docs)**; see "This repo's toolchain differs from TI's" below. From the R53 run, `ot-rcp`:

```text
ld: section .nvs VMA [0000000000010000,0000000000013fff] overlaps section .text VMA [0000000000000090,0000000000016213]
```

Every image is larger than the 64 kB below the settings area, so every image overlaps it. Seen for `ot-rcp` and `ot-cli-mtd` on the R53 and for `ot-rcp` and `ot-cli-radio` on the R52 (observed 2026-10-05; not saved; the radio CLI also reported a `.rodata` overlap there).

**Node builds on the R52, after the fix**, run out of RAM. **Unknown (suspected: Chip limit).** CLI MTD shown; the other node builds give the same pair with their own byte count:

```text
ld: bin/ot-cli-mtd.out section `.bss' will not fit in region `SRAM'
ld: region `SRAM' overflowed by 10216 bytes
```

Notes on the table:

- Flash counts code, read-only data and the copy of initialized data. RAM is the top of the stack minus the RAM base, so it includes the startup stack (2 kB) and the FreeRTOS heap (3.3 kB). Every number comes from the linker map, and the "over" numbers match the linker's own "overflowed by N bytes" lines.
- Flash is not the problem. The biggest image (CLI FTD) uses 417.5 kB of the 496 kB that sit below the settings area, 84%.
- R52 and R53 images are byte-for-byte the same size. Both build as device `cc23x0r5` with the same FreeRTOS settings. The only difference is the RAM region SysConfig writes into the linker map: `0x9000` (36 kB) for the R52, `0x10000` (64 kB) for the R53.
- The node builds configure on the R52 only after the board check is removed ("The gate"). The NCP rows need `-DNCP_BUILD_ENABLED=ON`.
- `-DNCP_BUILD_ENABLED=ON` also grows the CLI builds (it is a global define). With it on, the R52 CLI MTD is 10.5 kB over and CLI FTD 23.8 kB over. The CLI rows above are from the default build with it off.
- "Radio CLI" is a radio test tool, not a Thread node. It builds by default for this board.

### Where the RAM goes (R52 CLI MTD, from the map)

| Item | Bytes |
|---|---|
| `ot::Instance` (all of OpenThread's state, including 44 message buffers of 128 B = 5,632 B) | 12,256 |
| App task stack (`APP_STACK_SIZE` 2k words in `examples/apps/cli/freertos_main.c`) | 8,192 |
| CLI interpreter | 7,152 |
| FreeRTOS heap (`configTOTAL_HEAP_SIZE` 3400 for CC23X0R5) | 3,400 |
| FreeRTOS timer and idle task stacks and control blocks | 3,056 |
| Startup stack (linker script) | 2,048 |
| UART TX buffer | 1,024 |

The RCP needs none of the Thread state, which is why it fits. Getting an MTD under 36 kB would mean cutting about 7.5 kB from the NCP MTD (smaller app stack, fewer message buffers, smaller tables). That might be possible, but it is untested, it would be a custom configuration, and TI also lists sleepy end devices as unsupported on CC23xx (known issue TIOP-1452).

## The gate (what restricts the R52 to RCP)

**Tool or docs:** the build skips the node apps without a message. It is two CMake checks in `ot-ti`. Nothing in `boards.cmake` or `script/build` blocks it.

1. `examples/apps/cli/CMakeLists.txt`, lines 49 to 56:

   ```cmake
   if((OT_FTD) AND (NOT TI_SIMPLELINK_DEVICE STREQUAL "cc13x2_cc26x2") AND
       (NOT TI_SIMPLELINK_BOARD STREQUAL "LP_EM_CC2340R5"))
       include(ftd.cmake)
   endif()
   if((OT_MTD) AND (NOT TI_SIMPLELINK_DEVICE STREQUAL "cc13x2_cc26x2") AND
       (NOT TI_SIMPLELINK_BOARD STREQUAL "LP_EM_CC2340R5"))
   include(mtd.cmake)
   endif()
   ```

2. `examples/apps/CMakeLists.txt`, line 38: `if(NOT TI_SIMPLELINK_BOARD STREQUAL "LP_EM_CC2340R5")` around `add_subdirectory(ncp)`.

The libraries (`libopenthread-mtd.a`, `libopenthread-ftd.a`) build for the R52 even with the gate in place. Only the app executables are skipped. No warning is printed, so `./script/build LP_EM_CC2340R5` produces just `ot-rcp` and `ot-cli-radio` and says nothing about the rest.

## Local edits

Made in the local `ot-ti` clone only; the full diff is in `ot-ti-local.patch` in this folder.

1. Removed the R52 check from the FTD and MTD `if` lines in `examples/apps/cli/CMakeLists.txt`.
2. Changed the NCP check in `examples/apps/CMakeLists.txt` to `if(TRUE)`.
3. **Settings-area fix, needed for every image:** `src/cc23xx_cc27xx/openthread.syscfg` puts NVS at `0x10000` for all CC23xx parts, under a comment that says "place at the end of Flash". The smallest image is 96.1 kB, and `0x10000` is 64 kB from the start of flash, so code always runs into it. Moved to `0x7C000`, the last 16 kB of the 512 kB flash. Confirmed the original fails the same way on the R53 (`ot-rcp` and `ot-cli-mtd`), so it is not a side effect of the R52 or the gate.

## This repo's toolchain differs from TI's

Any of these could contribute to the settings-area link error above. **Unknown (suspected: Tool or docs).** The smallest image (96.1 kB) is about 32 kB larger than the space below the settings area (64 kB), a gap a compiler change is unlikely to close, but no build with TI's own toolchain was run.

- **Compiler:** GCC 12.2.0 from Zephyr SDK 0.17.4, not the GCC 9 (2020-q2) `ot-ti`'s build script expects, nor the Arm GNU 12.2.rel1 its bootstrap installs on Ubuntu.
- **SysConfig 1.26.3**, not the 1.27.0 `ot-ti` expects.
- **F3 SDK 9.20.00.86**, the submodule `ot-ti` pins (per its license file name), where TI's release notes say lpf3-9.20.00.81. The release notes and the pinned submodule disagree.

Full table under "Details".

## CCFG (debug and erase)

From the generated `ti_devices_config.c`, identical for every build:

- `allowDebugPort`, `allowChipErase`, `allowFlashProgram`, `allowFlashVerify`, `allowReturnToFactory`: all `CCFG_PERMISSION_ALLOW`
- `debugCfg.authorization = CCFG_DBGAUTH_DBGOPEN`, `allowBldr = CCFG_DBGBLDR_ALLOW`
- `chipEraseRetain` keeps no sectors (`0x0` and the required `0xF0000000`)
- Serial ROM bootloader disabled, `pAppVtor` = reset vectors at `0x0`
- **All CCFG CRC fields are 0.** **Tool or docs:** `ot-ti` has no post-build CRC step. The comment says the CRCs must be filled "as a post-build step, or by the flashloader". Whether UniFlash or CCStudio fills them at load time was not tested; the one flash here filled them first with upstream Zephyr's `soc/ti/simplelink/cc23x0/ti_ccfg_crc32_calculate.py`.

The images do not include the NVS area (it is `ALLOC` only), so flashing would not wipe stored settings beyond what the tool's erase does.

## Exact commands

Comments after `#` are notes and wall times, not part of the command. `otbuild.sh` and `mapmem.py` in the clone's `_tools/` folder are local helper scripts, not part of `ot-ti` and not in this repo.

```bash
git clone --depth 1 -b thread-v1.4-ti --recurse-submodules --shallow-submodules \
  https://github.com/TexasInstruments/ot-ti ~/ot-ti                     # 2 min 28 s

# Tools
mkdir -p ~/ot-ti/_tools/gcc/bin && cd ~/ot-ti/_tools/gcc/bin
for f in ~/zephyr-toolchain/arm-zephyr-eabi/bin/arm-zephyr-eabi-*; do
  n=$(basename $f); ln -sf $f ${n/arm-zephyr-eabi/arm-none-eabi}; done
python3 -m venv ~/ot-ti/_tools/venv && ~/ot-ti/_tools/venv/bin/pip install "cmake<4"
export PATH=$HOME/ot-ti/_tools/gcc/bin:$HOME/ot-ti/_tools/venv/bin:$PATH
export TI_SYSCONFIG_ROOT=/Applications/ti/sysconfig_1.26.3

# F3 SDK libraries (driverlib etc.), GCC only                            # 1 min 25 s
make -C ~/ot-ti/third_party/ti_simplelink_sdk/repo_cc23xx_cc27xx CMAKE=$(which cmake) \
  GCC_ARMCOMPILER=$HOME/ot-ti/_tools/gcc TICLANG_ARMCOMPILER= IAR_ARMCOMPILER= \
  SYSCONFIG_TOOL=/Applications/ti/sysconfig_1.26.3/sysconfig_cli.sh GENERATOR=Ninja

# Same configure and build as script/build (wrapper: ~/ot-ti/_tools/otbuild.sh <BOARD> <dir> [-D...])
cmake -GNinja -DOT_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=ON -DTI_SIMPLELINK_BOARD=LP_EM_CC2340R5 \
  -DOT_PLATFORM=external -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=src/arm-none-eabi-m0p.cmake ~/ot-ti -B _build/r5_default
cmake --build _build/r5_default -- -k 0
# NCP: add -DNCP_BUILD_ENABLED=ON. R53: -DTI_SIMPLELINK_BOARD=LP_EM_CC2340R53.

# Memory per image from the map: python3 ~/ot-ti/_tools/mapmem.py <RAM size> <map files>
```

`script/bootstrap` was read and **not run**: it downloads a Linux-only SysConfig `.run` installer, runs OpenThread's own bootstrap (Homebrew on a Mac), and uses `apt-get` and `sudo`. **Tool or docs** (no macOS path).

`script/build` was **not run as is**: it also rebuilds the whole F2 SDK (CC13xx and CC26xx, not needed for this board) and points at `/opt/gcc-arm-none-eabi-9-2020-q2-update`. The F3 SDK make step was run once by hand, then the same CMake command `script/build` uses.

## Attempts and wall times

| # | Attempt | Result | Wall time |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | R52 default, upstream source | Configure and compile OK. `ot-rcp` and `ot-cli-radio` fail to link on the `.nvs` overlap (log not saved; attempt 7 shows the same error) | 1 min 34 s |
| 2 | R52 default, NVS moved to `0x7C000` | Both link | 1 min 29 s |
| 3 | R52, FTD and MTD gate removed | Configure and compile OK. `ot-cli-mtd` overflowed by 10 kB, `ot-cli-ftd` by 16400 | 6 s (incremental) |
| 4 | R52, plus NCP gate removed, `-DNCP_BUILD_ENABLED=ON` | `ot-ncp-mtd` over by 7632, `ot-ncp-ftd` over by 21176, `ot-cli-mtd` over by 10768, `ot-cli-ftd` over by 24320 | 1 min 27 s |
| 5 | R53 default (FTD, MTD, RCP, radio CLI) | All four link | 1 min 28 s |
| 6 | R53, `-DNCP_BUILD_ENABLED=ON` | All six link | 2 min 6 s |
| 7 | R53, original NVS at `0x10000` | `ot-rcp` and `ot-cli-mtd` fail with the same `.nvs` overlap | 4 s (incremental) |

The full build logs were not kept.

## Trap: a huge .bin file

**Tool or docs.** Each app's post-build step runs `objcopy -O binary`. On CC23xx the image includes CCFG at `0x4E020000`, so the `.bin` fills the gap from `0x0` with zeros: `ot-rcp.bin` was 1.22 GB (1.2 GB). It was deleted after every build. Anyone building on a full disk will hit this. Use the `.out` or make a `.hex`.

## What to do next

- For a Thread end device or router on this chip family, use the CC2340R53 board (LP-EM-CC2340R53) or a CC27xx part. Neither has been run here.
- To use this board as an RCP, it needs a host running OpenThread's border router. `board-to-board/thread-two-radios-2026-10-06/` ran it with a Mac host: it joined a CC1354P10 leader.
- Find why the flashed radio CLI's serial output does not decode.

## Details

### Output files (LP_EM_CC2340R5, linked)

Built into `out/` in this folder, which is not in the repository. `ot-rcp` was flashed 2026-10-06 (CRCs filled) and ran; `ot-cli-radio` was flashed once, from a copy with its CRCs filled.

| File | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `out/ot-rcp.out`, `out/ot-rcp.hex`, `out/ot-rcp.map` | hex `5fc1b18061eadc895787fa236b8a37cb180c51fe394d0b32fe5642e0f629a162` |
| `out/ot-cli-radio.out`, `out/ot-cli-radio.hex`, `out/ot-cli-radio.map` | hex `946c2881649c77915975ba50822e70e6224cd3cb52752ef5e82666f17cfa6085` |

The `.hex` files were made with `arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O ihex` (`ot-ti` does not make them). Maps for the failed and R53 builds were not kept.

### Tools used, and differences from what `ot-ti` expects

| Tool | `ot-ti` expects | Used | Matters? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Arm GCC | `/opt/gcc-arm-none-eabi-9-2020-q2-update` (script default) or Arm GNU 12.2.rel1 (bootstrap, Ubuntu only) | Zephyr SDK 0.17.4 GCC 12.2.0 (`~/zephyr-toolchain/arm-zephyr-eabi`), linked as `arm-none-eabi-*` in `~/ot-ti/_tools/gcc/bin`. Has newlib nano for v6-m. | Compiled clean with warnings as errors. Sizes could differ a little from Arm's build of 12.2. No official toolchain download was needed. |
| SysConfig | 1.27.0 | 1.26.3 (`/Applications/ti/sysconfig_1.26.3`) | No version error or warning. Only warning was the default RNG noise conditioning key. |
| F3 SDK | lpf3-9.20.00.81 (release notes) | The submodule `ot-ti` pins, which is 9.20.00.86 (per its license file name). `/Applications/ti/simplelink_lowpower_f3_sdk_9_21_00_36_LTS` was not used. | The release notes and the pinned submodule disagree on the build number. |
| CMake | any | 3.31.10 from pip in `~/ot-ti/_tools/venv` (no system CMake on this Mac) | CMake 4 was avoided because the SDK uses old `cmake_minimum_required` lines. |
| Ninja, make, python3 | yes | already installed | |

### Disk

| Item | Size |
|---|---|
| Clone with submodules, as cloned | 4.0 GB (1.2 GB of it is `.git`, 2.5 GB the two SDKs) |
| `~/ot-ti` now (one build tree, tools, logs; unused F2 SDK working tree removed with `git submodule deinit`) | 3.4 GB |
| Peak during the run | 5.7 GB, plus 1.22 GB (1.2 GB) per `.bin` before deletion |
| One build tree | 520 to 710 MB |
| CMake venv | 133 MB |
| `thread/out/` | 7.7 MB |

The shallow clone alone is 4.0 GB, so plan for the peak above. To get the F2 SDK back:

```bash
git -C ~/ot-ti submodule update --init third_party/ti_simplelink_sdk/repo_cc13xx_cc26xx
```

To remove everything:

```text
rm -rf ~/ot-ti
```

==============================================================================
FILE: cc2340r5/zephyr-ti/README.md | Does Bluetooth LE work on the TI LP-EM-CC2340R5 with TI's Zephyr fork (simplelink-zephyr)?
==============================================================================

# Does Bluetooth LE work on the TI LP-EM-CC2340R5 with TI's Zephyr fork (simplelink-zephyr)?

Terms: Zephyr, west, CCFG, XDS110 and UniFlash are defined in [docs/vocab.md](../../docs/vocab.md). Errors and fixes: [FAQ.md](../FAQ.md).

**Update 2026-10-08: yes, with Zephyr's C library heap turned on** (`CONFIG_COMMON_LIBC_MALLOC_ARENA_SIZE=2048` in `prj.conf`; 1024 for the peripheral sample). The silent start below was TI's Bluetooth stack failing to get memory for a timer with the heap at 0. The BTHome beacon and the peripheral sample then ran with the fork's own CCFG byte; the beacon sample hard-faults. Details: [the experiment page](../../docs/experiments/2026-10-05-cc2340r5-ti-zephyr-ble.md). The rest of this page covers the build as first run on 2026-10-05, before the heap setting was found.

As first built on 2026-10-05, the Bluetooth samples printed nothing. TI's fork (tag `v3.7.0-ti-1.00.01_ga`) builds the Bluetooth beacon and peripheral samples with workarounds, and they flash, but nothing printed as built. hello_world printed its boot banner after CCFG byte 0x4E02001C was changed from 0x0F to 0x07 and all four checksums were recomputed; the Bluetooth samples, changed the same way, printed nothing, so it is not known whether they booted. **Unknown (suspected: Tool or docs):** the heap setting above is the suspected cause; it was found after these runs.

Contents: [results](#results), [hello_world ran after a boot-configuration change](#hello_world-ran-after-a-boot-configuration-change), [Bluetooth samples print nothing](#bluetooth-samples-print-nothing), [suspects](#suspects-where-this-setup-differs-from-tis), [versions](#versions), [commands and workarounds](#commands), [times](#times-wall-clock-machine-waiting), [disk](#disk), [lock check](#lock-check).

Tested 2026-10-05 on an Intel Mac (macOS 15.7.9) with the XDS110 probe and UniFlash 9.6.0. This is the Zephyr side of the comparison with TI's own SDK (FreeRTOS) Bluetooth build, which works ([../matrix/README.md](../matrix/README.md)).

The board carries the CC2340R52 chip, 36 kB of RAM; the CC2340R53 is a 64 kB version on a separate board, LP-EM-CC2340R53. 1 kB = 1,024 bytes; 1 GB = 1,024 MB.

> **Which file to flash.** TI's fork runs TI's CRC tool after the build (`ti-simplelink-crc-tool`, a Python program that computes the CCFG checksums, or CRCs, and writes them into the built file), so its `zephyr.hex` carries three of the four checksums: flash `zephyr.hex`. Upstream Zephyr 4.4.2 writes them into a separate `zephyr_crc32.hex`, so flash that one there. **Tool or docs:** the fork handles the checksums differently from upstream Zephyr, and its tool leaves the fourth at zero (see below). Never flash `zephyr.bin`: it is 1.22 GB (1.2 GB; see Disk).

## Results

| Sample | Flash used | RAM used | As built | With CCFG byte 0x4E02001C set to 0x07 |
|---|--:|--:|---|---|
| `samples/hello_world` | 30.6 kB | 8 kB (22.2%) | Flashed, no serial output | **Printed its boot banner:** `*** Booting Zephyr OS build cbababd4c1b4 *** Hello World! lp_em_cc2340r5/cc2340r5` (observed 2026-10-05; not saved) |
| `samples/bluetooth/beacon` | 110.2 kB (21.5%) | 28.4 kB (78.9%) | Flashed, no serial output, nothing on air | No serial output; `no adverts seen` in 30 s |
| `samples/bluetooth/peripheral` | 202.8 kB (39.6%) | 34.3 kB (95.3%) | Flashed, no serial output, nothing on air | No serial output; `no adverts seen` in 30 s |

Flash is out of 512 kB, RAM out of 36 kB. The peripheral sample fits only because TI ships a board file for it (`boards/lp_em_cc2340r5.conf`) that turns off settings, flash storage and the GATT cache. The beacon sample fits with no changes and has no board file. Every flash ended in UniFlash's `Success`.

"Nothing printed" was tested with the probe attached only. A power cycle with no probe was not run.

## hello_world ran after a boot-configuration change

**Unknown (suspected: Tool or docs).** Diffing the configuration area (CCFG, 0x4E020000) against an upstream Zephyr 4.4.2 image that runs on this board: the fork sets `misc` at 0x4E02001C to 0x0F, upstream to 0x07. The two builds also differ in Zephyr version (the fork is based on Zephyr 3.7.0, per its `VERSION` file; upstream was 4.4.2), so this byte is one difference among several, not the only one. The extra bit is `saciTimeoutOverride` (`hw_ccfg.h`), which makes the boot ROM use the configuration's own wait for a debugger command instead of the factory one. hello_world printed its boot banner after CCFG byte 0x4E02001C was changed from 0x0F to 0x07 and all four checksums were recomputed (observed 2026-10-05; not saved). The setting may be meant for a power-up without a probe, which was not tested.

The change, as run here. It uses the `intelhex` Python package, which upstream Zephyr's Python environment includes, and upstream Zephyr's checksum script. Replace `~/zephyrproject` with your upstream Zephyr workspace and `build/zephyr/zephyr.hex` with your build's hex.

```bash
python3 -c "from intelhex import IntelHex; b=IntelHex('build/zephyr/zephyr.hex'); b[0x4E02001C]=0x07; b.write_hex_file('zephyr_misc07.hex')"
```

```bash
python3 ~/zephyrproject/zephyr/soc/ti/simplelink/cc23x0/ti_ccfg_crc32_calculate.py zephyr_misc07.hex zephyr_fixed.hex
```

```bash
/Applications/ti/uniflash_9.6.0/dslite.sh --mode flash -c CC2340R5.ccxml -e -f -u zephyr_fixed.hex
```

The other CCFG differences from upstream are the user-record CRC the fork leaves at zero and debug in the boot loader (`allowBldr`, 0x00 here, 0xA5 upstream). The user record is a 128-byte area at 0x4E020750 in the CCFG for the application's own data; its last word is a CRC over the rest. TI's `hw_ccfg.h` says the boot code has "no dependencies" on it and calls that CRC optional. Filling only the user-record CRC, with upstream's script on the unchanged beacon image, did not make it run. The hello_world image that printed its banner had the byte changed and all four CRCs filled by upstream's script, so the byte change with the user-record CRC still at zero was not tested. `allowBldr` was left as the fork sets it.

## Bluetooth samples print nothing

**Unknown.** With the same boot-configuration change, beacon and peripheral print nothing, not even Zephyr's boot banner, and nothing is seen on air in 30 seconds, so it is not known whether they booted. The interrupt control register showed no fault in progress; suspected: the code waits in early start-up (a clock or the radio), but that was not checked.

## Suspects: where this setup differs from TI's

Any of these could be why the Bluetooth samples print nothing. None is proven.

- **Compiler.** GCC 12.2 from Zephyr SDK 0.17.4, reused from the upstream Zephyr run through `cross-compile`, not TI's tested toolchain.
- **lief 1.0.0 instead of 0.12.3.** `lief` is a Python library that reads and rewrites compiled program files; TI's CRC tool uses it to write the checksums into the built file. The tool was written for lief 0.12.3 and ran here with 1.0.0 (workaround in step 5 below). The output CRCs agree with an independent calculation, but lief rewrote the ELF file (the compiled program the hex is made from), and the rest of the image was not compared against an unpatched one.
- **User-record CRC left at 0 by TI's tool.** TI's CRC tool patches three CRCs (boot config, main CCFG, debug config). Upstream Zephyr's script also writes a fourth, the user record's CRC at 0x4E0207CC. The three shared CRCs match the upstream script byte for byte. Filling the fourth alone did not help, and the hello_world image that printed its banner had it filled. TI's `hw_ccfg.h` says the boot code does not depend on the user record; that was not tested on the chip.
- **The objcopy path patch** (step 6 below), a one-line local change to the fork's build. `objcopy` is the GNU tool that copies a built program into other file formats, such as `.hex` and `.bin`.

Other limits:

- **The peripheral sample has 1.7 kB of RAM left.** **Chip limit.** Adding anything (logging, a second service, bonding) will likely overflow.
- **`west flash` supports only J-Link for this board**, per the fork's README ("only JLink is available"). **Tool or docs**, because here it is TI's fork and TI's README. Upstream Zephyr 4.4.2 has the same J-Link-only flash setup for this board; the FAQ tags that one **Third-party behavior** because upstream is not TI's. Flash with UniFlash and the XDS110 probe instead, as above.

## Versions

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Repo | <https://github.com/TexasInstruments/simplelink-zephyr> |
| Tag | `v3.7.0-ti-1.00.01_ga` (commit `cbababd4`). Newest GA tag on 2026-10-05. Newer `9.x` tags exist but are all `_ea` (early access) or `-internal`, so they were not used. |
| HAL | `simplelink-hal_ti` at `ab1817da` ("simplelink_lpf3: 218d961-ti-v1.00 release") |
| Other modules | `cmsis` `4b96cbb1`, `mbedtls` `2f24831e`, `tinycrypt` `1012a3eb` |
| Compiler | `~/zephyr-toolchain/arm-zephyr-eabi` (GCC 12.2 from Zephyr SDK 0.17.4), via `cross-compile` |
| Python | 3.12 venv at `~/zephyr-ti/.venv` |
| CRC tool | `ti-simplelink-crc-tool` 1.2.5.0 from PyPI, run with `lief` 1.0.0 (see step 5) |

## Commands

Steps that differ from TI's README are marked OVERRIDE. Comments after `#` are notes, not commands.

```bash
# 1. Python and west. 32 s.
mkdir -p ~/zephyr-ti && cd ~/zephyr-ti
python3.12 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install --upgrade pip west cmake

# 2. Workspace at the GA tag, shallow. 31 s.
west init -m https://github.com/TexasInstruments/simplelink-zephyr \
  --mr v3.7.0-ti-1.00.01_ga --clone-opt=--depth=1 ~/zephyr-ti/ws

# 3. Only the modules this build needs. OVERRIDE: project filter. 18 s total (11 s, then 7 s for the two crypto modules the first build asked for).
cd ~/zephyr-ti/ws
west config manifest.project-filter -- '-.*,+simplelink-hal_ti,+cmsis,+mbedtls,+tinycrypt'
west update --narrow -o=--depth=1

# 4. Python packages. 12 s.
pip install -r zephyr/scripts/requirements-base.txt

# 5. OVERRIDE: TI's CRC tool. It is listed only in requirements-extras.txt, and it pins
#    lief 0.12.3, which has no wheel for Python 3.12 on an Intel Mac and fails to build.
#    Install the tool without its pins and use a current lief wheel. Under a minute, not timed.
pip install --only-binary=:all: lief
pip download --no-deps -d ~/zephyr-ti/_pkgs ti-simplelink-crc-tool
pip install --no-deps ~/zephyr-ti/_pkgs/ti_simplelink_crc_tool-1.2.5.0-py3-none-any.whl

# 6. OVERRIDE: the fork's CC23xx post-build step calls objcopy at a fixed Zephyr SDK path.
#    Point it at the active compiler's objcopy instead (one-line local patch, not committed anywhere).
sed -i '' 's#${ZEPHYR_SDK_INSTALL_DIR}/arm-zephyr-eabi/bin/arm-zephyr-eabi-objcopy#${CMAKE_OBJCOPY}#' \
  zephyr/soc/ti/simplelink/cc23x0/CMakeLists.txt

# 7. Build. 60 s and 63 s from clean.
export ZEPHYR_TOOLCHAIN_VARIANT=cross-compile
export CROSS_COMPILE=$HOME/zephyr-toolchain/arm-zephyr-eabi/bin/arm-zephyr-eabi-
cd ~/zephyr-ti/ws/zephyr
west build -p always -b lp_em_cc2340r5 samples/bluetooth/peripheral -d ~/zephyr-ti/build-peripheral
west build -p always -b lp_em_cc2340r5 samples/bluetooth/beacon     -d ~/zephyr-ti/build-beacon
```

The workarounds, with the error each one avoids:

- **Step 5, lief.** **Tool or docs.** Without it, installing the CRC tool with its pins fails with `ERROR: Failed to build 'lief' when getting requirements to build wheel`. Without the CRC tool at all (it is not in `requirements-base.txt`), the build links and then stops at `/bin/sh: crc_tool: command not found`.
- **Step 6, objcopy.** **Tool or docs.** The fork's `soc/ti/simplelink/cc23x0/CMakeLists.txt` runs `${ZEPHYR_SDK_INSTALL_DIR}/arm-zephyr-eabi/bin/arm-zephyr-eabi-objcopy`, a path that exists only with a full Zephyr SDK install. Setting `ZEPHYR_SDK_INSTALL_DIR` to work around it made Zephyr look for a full SDK and stop in `FindZephyr-sdk.cmake` (**Our mistake**). The exact error text of both stops was not saved.
- **Step 3, module filter.** **Our mistake.** The first filter left out `mbedtls` and `tinycrypt`, and Kconfig (Zephyr's build-time settings system, the `CONFIG_...` options) stopped. The filter above includes them. The exact Kconfig error text was not saved.

The manifest has a group meant for TI staff only. It is off by default (`group-filter` in `west.yml`), and the project filter above does not turn it on: `+simplelink-hal_ti` matches only that one project name. Do not add a bare `hal_ti` pattern to the filter.

## Times (wall clock, machine waiting)

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| venv plus west and CMake | 32 s |
| `west init` (shallow) | 31 s |
| `west update` (4 modules, shallow) | 18 s |
| `requirements-base.txt` | 12 s |
| CRC tool plus lief | under 1 min, not timed |
| Build, peripheral (clean) | 60 s |
| Build, beacon (clean) | 63 s |

Three failed build attempts came first: the Kconfig stop on missing mbedtls and tinycrypt (18 s), `crc_tool: command not found` after a good link (66 s), and the Zephyr SDK lookup triggered by setting `ZEPHYR_SDK_INSTALL_DIR` (11 s). They are not counted above.

## Disk

| Path | Size |
|---|---|
| `~/zephyr-ti/ws` (zephyr plus 4 modules) | 663 MB |
| `~/zephyr-ti/.venv` | 179 MB |
| `~/zephyr-ti/build-peripheral` | 40 MB |
| `~/zephyr-ti/build-beacon` | 33 MB |
| **`~/zephyr-ti` total** | **915 MB** |

The compiler is shared with the upstream run and not counted. `zephyr.bin` in each build folder is 1.22 GB (1.2 GB) because it spans from address 0 to the end of the configuration area, which starts at 0x4E020000. It is a sparse file: `du` shows 208 kB or less on disk for each one here. Do not copy it with a tool that fills sparse files, and do not flash it. Use the hex.

## Lock check

Can these images lock the chip? No: every permission is set to allow. TI's fork sets the chip's configuration area (CCFG) from Kconfig, not devicetree. Both Bluetooth builds have:

```text
CONFIG_CC23X0_ALLOW_DEBUG_PORT=y
CONFIG_CC23X0_ALLOW_ENERGY_TRACE=y
CONFIG_CC23X0_ALLOW_FLASH_VERIFY=y
CONFIG_CC23X0_ALLOW_FLASH_PROGRAM=y
CONFIG_CC23X0_ALLOW_CHIP_ERASE=y
CONFIG_CC23X0_ALLOW_TOOLS_CLIENT_MODE=y
CONFIG_CC23X0_ALLOW_RETURN_TO_FACTORY=y
```

In the hex, the permission word at 0x4E020018 is `aaaaaaaa` (every permission set to allow), and debug authorization at 0x4E0207D0 is `0x5A` (debug open). Main flash sectors are not write-protected (`0xffffffff`). The CCFG sector write-protect mask is 0, the same value as the upstream blinky image that flashed and ran on this board. No "LOCK YOUR DEVICE" warning was printed. The fork's sources do not contain that check at all, so its absence proves nothing by itself; the values above are what was checked.

# Zephyr on the LP-EM-CC2340R5 with the XDS110 probe

Terms: [docs/vocab.md](../../docs/vocab.md). Errors and fixes: [FAQ.md](../FAQ.md). 1 kB = 1,024 bytes.

Works: Zephyr 4.4.2 `samples/basic/blinky` runs on the LP-EM-CC2340R5. It took 82 seconds from the first command to the program printing on the serial port (2026-10-05). The serial port shows the LED state changing every second, and the green LED was seen blinking.

The LED is the **green** one. Zephyr's board file makes green `led0`, and blinky uses `led0`. The SDK example that was on the board before blinks red, so a green blink also proves the new program is the one running.

## Times

| Step | Seconds |
|---|--:|
| Read the board file, check the workspace, measure disk | 16 |
| Build (clean) | 47 |
| Check the image before flashing | 12 |
| Flash and start | 7 |
| **Total** | **82** |

Nothing new was downloaded: the Zephyr workspace and compiler (944 MB and 1.1 GB) were already on the Mac. This build added 34 MB. The first-time install of both is in [mac-setup/README.md](../../mac-setup/README.md).

## Manual overrides

| # | The official way | What blocked it | What was done instead |
|---|------------------|-----------------|-----------------------|
| 1 | `west flash`, per the Zephyr board page ("flashed in the usual way") | The board's flash setup lists J-Link only. The probe sold for this board is an XDS110. The prebuilt OpenOCD used for the MSPM0 board has no CC23xx support. | UniFlash command line with the connection file from this repo. |
| 2 | Flash `zephyr.hex` | The chip's boot code checks checksums in its configuration area. The build writes a second file, `zephyr_crc32.hex`, with them filled in. `west flash` picks that file on its own; a person flashing by hand has to know. | Flashed `zephyr_crc32.hex`. |
| 3 | Flash with verify | Verify reports one mismatch at 0x4E020750 (expected 0x00, read 0xFF). Same address with the SDK image and the Zephyr image. | Treated as a tool or chip quirk, not a bad flash: both programs run. Cause still open. |

## Safety check before flashing

Zephyr's source for this chip warns that an image built without the chip-erase permission "will LOCK YOUR DEVICE." Before flashing, the built device tree was checked: debug port, flash program, chip erase and return to factory are all allowed, and the build printed no lock warning. The image was also checked to contain only the program area (0x0 to 0x277C) and the configuration area (0x4E020000 to 0x4E020800).

## Repeat it

`./setup-intel-mac.sh` installs Zephyr if it is not there, builds, checks the named probe is connected, flashes and resets. Set `ZP`, `TC` and `PROBE_SERIAL` to choose folders and the board.

## What you see

The build's memory report is flash 9.9 kB and RAM 4 kB. After reset the serial port prints `LED state: ON` and `LED state: OFF` one second apart, and the green LED toggles with it.

Next: Bluetooth on this board needs TI's Zephyr fork; see [zephyr-ti](../zephyr-ti/README.md).
